_comment: v1.12.0 - the first De Bello Civili batch: Book I (10 new, joining the launch-era I.7 for 11). All ten are whole chapters, so no citation names its subsections. The arc of the book in ten stops: the motives (4), the senatus consultum ultimum and the flight of the tribunes (5), the peace terms and the dignitas crux (9), Corfinium twice - the war aims stated over a man begging for his life (22) and the clemency (23) - Pompey leaving Italy from Brundisium (28), the chapter in which Caesar does not mention robbing the treasury (33), the refusal to fight a battle he could win (72), the two camps becoming one (74), and Petreius ending that with an oath and a killing (76). Source defect: I.23 prints `Frentranorum` for `Frentanorum`.
bc.1.9: Quae res etsi nihil ad levandas
